issues.failure_explanation: Theorem thm:overparam is given no proof; its only support is the sentence deriving pi from eq:gibbs via x=u⊙v, η=u⊙u/2. Substituting these gives x_i^2/(2η_i)=v_i^2 and β^2λ^2η_i/2=β^2λ^2u_i^2/4, i.e. the density u·exp(-v^2-β^2λ^2u^2/4-βG), which is not pi's exp(-βλ(u^2+v^2)/2) unless βλ=2. The correct substitution is η_i=u_i^2/(βλ) (a rescaling u→a u, v→v/a with a^2=2/(βλ)). The theorem's conclusions (marginal ρ and the constant sqrt(π/(2βλ))^d) are nevertheless correct by direct integration.

failure_location.quote: $x = u \odot v$ and $\eta = u \odot u/2$ to \eqref{eq:gibbs}

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace η=u⊙u/2 by η=u⊙u/(βλ) (or add the rescaling) and/or include the one-line marginal integration using eq:laplace with a=sqrt(βλ), z=sqrt(βλ)x.
issues.overall_effect: The derivation offered for the central reparameterisation is incorrect as written; the theorem itself remains true but is unsupported in the text.
issues.title: Stated change of variables does not produce the density pi (theorem left without valid derivation)
issues.why_classification: Routine local correction; all conclusions of the theorem survive unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The integrand on the right-hand side is bounded for $\epsilon>0$ by part 1 with $r=2-2\epsilon<2$.

issues.failure_explanation: Burkholder–Davis–Gundy gives E|∫u^{ε-1}dW|^q ≤ c E[(∫_0^T u^{2ε-2}dt)^{q/2}]. For q>2 the map x↦x^{q/2} is convex, so E[(∫X)^{q/2}] ≥ (∫E X)^{q/2}; the paper's replacement of the expectation of the power by the power of the expectation is an invalid inference. Bounding E[(∫u^{2ε-2})^{q/2}] directly via Jensen the other way needs E u^{-(2-2ε)q/2}<∞, i.e. q<2/(1-ε), so for large q the quantity needed is exactly of the type being proved (part 2 with exponent 2-2ε).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Bootstrap: prove part 2 for q≤2 (Jensen is valid there), then for q∈(2,4] use the q/2-moment of ∫u^{-(2-2ε)} from the previous step with ε'=2ε, and iterate in q.
issues.overall_effect: As written, part 2 of Corollary cor is established only for q≤2 (or small q); the all-q claim, used by Proposition timeregbnd and the discretisation error analysis, lacks a valid proof step.
issues.title: BDG step in Corollary cor part 2 applies Jensen in the wrong direction for q>2
issues.why_classification: A short inductive argument using the paper's own estimates closes the gap with no loss of content.

issues.failure_explanation: The singular drift ∫_s^t u^{-1}dr is controlled by Hölder with exponent (1-ε)/(2-ε)<1/2, and E u_t^{-q} is infinite for q≥2 so an exponent exactly 1/2 cannot be obtained this way. The proof concludes with |t-s|^{1/2-ε}, not |t-s|^{1/2}; the statement's q/2 is not supported.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate part 1 with exponent q(1/2-ε) for any ε∈(0,1/2).
issues.overall_effect: Statement of part 1 overstates the Hölder exponent; downstream uses (part 2, Proposition prop:error_under_bounded_ball) only need 1/2-ε and already carry an ε-loss, so no downstream result changes.
issues.title: Proposition timeregbnd part 1 claims exponent q/2 but proof yields q(1/2-ε)
issues.why_classification: Correcting the exponent is local and every dependent estimate already tolerates the ε-loss.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: By \cite[Corollary 5.14]{Karatzas1991-xr}, it is enough to find an $\epsilon>0$ such that, for all $t\in [0,T]$,
the condition on $\alpha$ is satisfied if $\epsilon  <\beta\lambda/(2\gamma \cinfty^2)$

issues.failure_explanation: The proof only shows E exp(γ∫_t^{t+ε}‖b‖^2)<∞ for a short window ε<βλ/(2γB^2), which (via Karatzas–Shreve Cor. 5.14) implies the exponential martingale property but not the displayed global exponential moment. The global statement is in fact false in general: ‖b‖^2 is comparable to B^2‖z‖^2 and for OU-type processes E exp(γ∫_0^T‖z‖^2) is infinite once γ exceeds a T-dependent threshold.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the lemma as: M_T is a true martingale (Novikov's condition holds in the localized form of Karatzas–Shreve Cor. 5.14); keep the proof.
issues.overall_effect: The lemma as stated is wrong for large γ; only the martingale property (which is all Girsanov and Proposition prop:added-1 use) is actually proved.
issues.title: Lemma lem:novikov asserts exponential integrability for all γ, proof only establishes the local Novikov criterion
issues.why_classification: Weakening the statement to what is proved costs nothing downstream; all uses need only the martingale property.

issues.failure_explanation: From the proof's own μ, μ_1 = -2λη - x∇G/2 + 1, whereas (-M∇H)_1 = -η(2λ - λx^2/(8η^2) + 1/(2η)) - (x/2)(∇G + λx/(4η)) = -2λη - x∇G/2 - 1/2. Hence μ - (-M∇H) = (3/2, x/(2η)) (the Euclidean row-divergence of M, consistent with the paper's later Fokker–Planck computation), not (1/2, x/(2η)) as claimed. Moreover, with det M = 4η^2 per component, the paper's definition of div_g with g=M^{-1} gives div_{M^{-1}}(M) = Σ_j∂_jM_{ij} - M_{iη}/η = (1/2, 0), which matches neither expression. Thus the SDE displayed in the proposition is incorrect, and the process is not the Riemannian Langevin diffusion eq:riemannian for H with metric M^{-1} (that diffusion has Lebesgue-invariant density e^{-H}|g|^{1/2} ∝ e^{-H}/η, not e^{-H}).

failure_location.quote: d\mathbf{z}_t = - M(\mathbf{z}_t) \nabla H(\mathbf{z}_t)\, dt +\mathrm{div}_{M(\mathbf{z}_t)^{-1}}\pa{  M(\mathbf{z}_t)}\, dt  + \sqrt{2} S(\mathbf{z}_t) dW_t,

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace div_{M^{-1}}(M) in the statement and proof by the Euclidean row-divergence div(M) = (3/2, x/(2η)), correct the identity for μ, and reword the correspondence: the dynamics are Riemannian Langevin with metric M^{-1} for the potential H + (1/2)log det M^{-1} (equivalently the Lebesgue-reference form of Riemannian Langevin), not for H itself.
issues.overall_effect: The displayed drift identity in prop:added-2 is false and the advertised correspondence with Riemannian Langevin dynamics (eq:riemannian) for the potential H does not hold as stated; the Fokker–Planck equation ∂_tρ = div(M∇(H+log ρ)ρ) remains correct. No other result depends on this proposition.
issues.title: Wrong correction drift in Proposition prop:added-2: μ ≠ -M∇H + (1/2)(1, x/η) and neither equals div_{M^{-1}}(M)
issues.why_classification: The fix is contained, but a displayed equation of the proposition is false and the stated interpretation as Riemannian Langevin for H must be weakened/modified; the FP conclusion survives.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: applies to the potential $\frac 12 \lambda \|\vec x \|^2+G_3(\vec x)$, as it is a bounded perturbation (given by $G$) of a convex potential

issues.failure_explanation: The invariant law is ∝ exp(-β(λ‖x‖^2/2 + G_3)). The Gaussian factor exp(-βλ‖x‖^2/2) satisfies LSI(βλ); the perturbation is βG_3 with oscillation β(sup G - inf G), so Holley–Stroock yields R = βλ e^{-β(sup G - inf G)}. The stated constant drops the factor β in the exponent and is not the value the cited argument produces (it agrees only when β=1).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace R by βλ exp(-β(sup G - inf G)).
issues.overall_effect: The quantitative rate in eq. hhh is misstated for β≠1; geometric convergence itself is unaffected.
issues.title: LSI constant in Theorem thm_bndd_G omits the factor β in the Holley–Stroock exponent
issues.why_classification: A one-symbol correction to a constant; the qualitative theorem and all dependents survive.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: By  \cref{lem:2ndmoments_discrete}, the transition kernel satisfies a Lyapunov condition.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof's Lyapunov condition comes from Lemma lem:2ndmoments_discrete, which needs Δt<λ/B² to make α=(1+Δt²B²)/(1+λΔt)²<1. For large Δt with B>λ this contraction fails (Δt²B² > (1+λΔt)²-1), so the theorem as stated for all Δt under reg1 alone is not established.

failure_location.quote: Under \cref{reg1}, the distribution $P^k(X_0,\cdot)$ of the numerical approximation $x^k$  converges to the invariant distribution $\pi_{\deltat}$ geometrically.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis Δt<λ/B² (vacuous if B=0) to the statement of num_erg.
issues.overall_effect: Geometric ergodicity of the scheme is proved only for Δt<λ/B²; the theorem's unrestricted statement is unsupported.
issues.title: Theorem num_erg omits the stepsize restriction Δt<λ/B² required by its Lyapunov lemma
issues.why_classification: Adding the standard stepsize condition already present in the lemma preserves the result for the regime of interest (small Δt).

diagnostic_evidence.quote: follow an initial distribution $\rho_0\ll \pi $ such that $\frac{\rho_0}{\pi}$ is uniformly bounded.
An easy corollary of \cref{lem:2ndmoments_discrete} is that  $\pi_\tstep(V)$ (for $V((u,v))=1+\norm{(u,v)}^2$) is bounded uniformly in $\tstep$.

issues.failure_explanation: Theorem thm:num_conv is a limit statement for a fixed initial law ρ_0 whose constants (through Corollary cor, Proposition timeregbnd via ‖ρ_0/π‖_∞, and E Z_0^p) depend on ρ_0. In the proof the initial law is π̃_Δt (π_Δt truncated to a ball of radius Δt^{-1}), which changes with Δt. Concluding E_{1,T}(Δt)→0 therefore requires (a) that ‖π̃_Δt/π‖_∞ (and E_{π̃_Δt}Z_0^p) be bounded uniformly in Δt and (b) that the convergence in thm:num_conv be uniform over such a class; neither is shown, and it is not even verified that π̃_Δt/π is bounded. Additionally, the step from π̃_Δt(P^k_Δt φ) to π_Δt(φ)=π_Δt(P^k_Δt φ) needs control of P^k_Δt φ on the complement of the ball under π_Δt, for which only π_Δt(V) bounded is available (this gives π_Δt(B_R^c)→0 but not π_Δt(V1_{B_R^c})→0).

failure_location.quote: If $\pi_\tstep$ does not satisfy \cref{reg3}, we may replace $\pi_\tstep$ with  a regularised distribution $\tilde \pi_\tstep$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Establish uniform-in-Δt bounds on ‖π̃_Δt/π‖_∞ and higher moments of π_Δt, and make the constants in Corollary cor, Proposition timeregbnd and Propositions prop:error_under_bounded_ball/prop:error_discrete explicit in ‖ρ_0/π‖_∞ so that thm:num_conv holds uniformly over the class; alternatively run the triangle-inequality argument from the fixed initial law π (h_0≡1) using a Δt-uniform version of the discrete ergodicity constants in num_erg.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of convergence of π_Δt to π (a main advertised contribution in the abstract and conclusion) has a genuine gap; the conclusion is plausible but not established by the arguments given.
issues.title: Convergence of invariant measures applies the finite-time limit theorem to Δt-dependent initial laws without uniformity
issues.why_classification: A contained but nontrivial new lemma (uniform density/moment or uniform ergodicity bounds) is needed; no rate is claimed, so the qualitative result is recoverable without new global architecture.
